tier_reason: The README's walking-silhouettes table gives Boost.Geometry discrete Hausdorff at 12382.56 ms vs 50.48 ms for the method (245x), and the benchmark code is public (HausdorffDistanceOptimized/src/baselines, main.cpp, scripts/run_benchmarks.*). No hardware or explicit flags are stated (README, docs/article.html) and the measurement is first-party, so C; the >50x gain with unstated flags also caps it at C.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: CMake Release build: Windows preset x64-release (Visual Studio 2026 toolchain, Ninja, vcpkg) or Linux -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release with GCC/Ninja. Which toolchain produced the published numbers, and the explicit optimization flags, are not stated.
corrections.caveats: First-party benchmark; hardware not stated in the README or the article (docs/article.html). The speedup exploits contour ordering that Boost's general function cannot use, so it is a specialised-input comparison. Without BOOST_GEOMETRY_ENABLE_SIMILARITY_RTREE (not defined in this build), Boost's discrete_hausdorff_distance is a plain O(n*m) scan with no early break. The author's own shuffled brute force is already about 15x faster than Boost on the same package (821.73 vs 12382.56 ms, derived from page data), and the method beats that by 16.3x. The Boost timing includes converting contours to Boost linestrings on every call (CalcHausdorffDistanceBoost). Boost is reported only for the walking-silhouette package; the article says Boost was used mainly as a correctness reference. On Kimia216 the method only ties shuffled brute force (813.40 vs 812.02 ms). The README also lists an OpenCV FLANN kd-tree baseline, which the article says is not strictly exact. Very new repo (first commit 2026-05-14, 10 commits, 1 star).

notes: Numbers match the README. Metadata checked on the repo page: MIT, 1 star, not a fork, last commit 2026-06-01. The GitHub Pages article host (kate-droid-cpu.github.io) is egress-blocked, so the same article was read from raw docs/article.html.

CGAL, the named incumbent, is not in the comparison. Very new repo (oldest visible commit 2026-08-02, 48 commits).

corrections.claimed_speedup: README charts only (values read off the images, approximate): insertion on MARINE at capacity 512 about 31.8 s (Boost) vs about 25 s (Indexicon), roughly 20% less time; range query on MARINE at capacity 32 about 425 ms vs about 280 ms (roughly 34% less); TORONTO queries at capacity 32 about 38.5 ms vs about 30.5 ms. Near parity for OSM insertion at capacities 32-64, MIAMI insertion at 32 and TIGER queries at 32-128. Indexicon is at or below Boost in every plotted point (derived from page data).

corrections.caveats: Own benchmark against Boost only, shown as chart images. The Boost comparison harness is not in the repo (test/ holds usage examples only).
